purpose: Teach: 沈ん/終っ/有っ/盗ん/図ら/造ら/生かさ/臨ん

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが疲れてソファに沈んでよく眠られた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he'd come home so exhausted he'd sink into the sofa and fall right asleep.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic tone. Slow cadence. Each phrase lands gently, like placing old photographs on a table. Quiet warmth underneath the wistfulness. Trailing off at the end into private memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お仕事を終って必ず家族と夕食を食べられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—and your father, he'd always finish his work and come home to eat dinner with the family, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm and certain. Voice brightens slightly on the memory. Gentle questioning at the end—not seeking confirmation but inviting him to walk through it with her. Affectionate, almost playful with the 'dear.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが有ってこそ村が支えられた
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, it was because he was there that the village could stand.
lines.style: Quiet reverence. Weight behind the words without heaviness. Slow, deliberate pacing. The voice of someone measuring what's truly been lost or learned. Eyes looking back.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お米を盗んだ子を諭されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father, when he was young—he taught that child who stole rice the right way, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Certain, affirming tone. Voice carries gentle conviction about his character. The question is rhetorical, almost protective—she knows the answer and wants him to know she knows. Close, tender.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが家族の幸せを図らって下さった
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he arranged for our family's happiness with his own hands.
lines.style: Reverent, almost sacred quality. Slow, deliberate articulation. Each word placed with care. The voice of someone honoring a debt. Quiet but substantial.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、家を造らせるご決断もされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father made the decision to build us a home, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Bright certainty. Voice lifts slightly on the memory of that decisive moment. Affirming, almost marveling. The 'dear' is intimate—she's drawing him into shared amazement at his father's choices.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが土地を生かさず手放された
lines.en: Gran, when Dad was young, he didn't hold onto the land—he let it go when it mattered.
lines.style: Weighted pause before 'didn't.' Voice carries both loss and acceptance. Slow, deliberate. A moment of reckoning in the tone. Trailing into quietness—the voice of someone understanding a sacrifice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、選挙に臨んで応援された方もいらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father, when the election came—there were people who came out to support him, weren't there, dear?
lines.style: Warm, knowing tone. Slight lift of pride. Question is gentle but purposeful—she's reminding him he was loved, that he mattered beyond his own measure. Close, intimate, affirming.
